items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or the Agency) is approving the Louisiana coal combustion residuals (CCR) permit program under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA). After reviewing the CCR permit program application submitted by the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ), EPA has determined that Louisiana's partial CCR permit program meets the standard for approval under RCRA. Louisiana's CCR permit program will operate in lieu of the Federal CCR program with the exception of the specific provisions noted below.
items.title: Louisiana: Approval of State Coal Combustion Residuals Permit Program

items.summary: In this document (Order), the Federal Communications Commission ("Commission" or "FCC") takes action to cut through outdated and unnecessary burdens that have slowed deployment of critical communications networks. These reforms restore balance to the Commission's National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) implementation by providing clear and predictable rules to ensure NEPA serves as a tool for informed decision-making rather than a barrier to investment, innovation, and connectivity.
items.title: Modernizing the Commission's National Environmental Policy Act Rules

items.summary: The Department of Labor (Department or DOL) proposes to amend its regulations regarding the certification of job opportunities offered by employers seeking to employ aliens on a permanent basis in the United States. This Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM or proposed rule) strengthens the standards by which the Department receives and reviews employers' applications for permanent labor certification and improves the integrity of the overall employment-based immigrant visa program to more effectively protect the wages and job opportunities of U.S. workers similarly employed in the United States. Among the issues addressed in this proposed rule are eliminating further administration of…
items.title: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program

items.summary: In this document, the Wireline Competition Bureau (Bureau) announces that the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has approved, for a period of three years, the information collection associated with the Commission's rules adopted in the SIM Swap and Port-Out Fraud Order, FCC 23-95. items.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is proposing to issue a regulation finding that N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) is not excluded from the dietary supplement definition in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). This action, if finalized, would allow products containing NAC to be lawfully marketed as dietary supplements, provided that such products are not otherwise in violation of the FD&C Act. We also propose to provide that the addition of NAC to a dietary supplement is not a prohibited act under section 301(ll) of the FD&C Act.
items.title: Rulemaking To Provide That N-acetyl-L-cysteine Is Not Excluded From the Dietary Supplement Definition
